opportunity: Medicaid Recovery Audit Contractor delivered as software (AI claims analytics + automated medical-record review, contingency-priced)
buyer: State Medicaid agency / program integrity unit
mandate: SSA 1902(a)(42)(B); 42 CFR 455 Subpart F (12.5% contingency cap)
failure_evidence: Zero-bid RFPs recorded in CMS-approved SPAs: DE, SC, ID (3 RFPs), MO (incumbent declined), MN, AL (2017 & 2022), MT, ND, WY, PA. GAO-23-106025: 21 states + DC cite inability to procure; only 16 states run a RAC.; CMS is itself piloting OCR/ML/NLP for medical-record review (one-offer $2.29M award to ePathUSA, Feb 2026)
gap_type: Unit economics broken for labor-based auditors under the fee cap in small, managed-care-heavy states
ai_cost_lever: High - the thing that kills bids is the per-review labor cost; LLM chart review + claims rules drop it by an order of magnitude
key_risk: Mandate is soft: CMS routinely grants 2-yr exemptions, so the state must want recoveries; provider/legislative pushback on audits; 3-yr lookback & record-request limits in some states
sources: GAO-23-106025; CMS SPA exemption compendium (mjsimonandcompany.com States-Medicaid-RAC-Programs.pdf); USAspending 75FCMC26C0007

opportunity: Medicaid managed-care secret shopper + provider-directory accuracy surveys (AI voice + directory reconciliation)
buyer: State Medicaid agency (must be independent of the agency and the plans)
mandate: 42 CFR 438.68(f) & 457.1218 (2024 Access rule); first rating period on/after 9 Jul 2028; directory errors to state within 3 days
failure_evidence: Pre-failure: new mandate, 44 states / 629 MCO-PIHP-PAHPs, supply today is a handful of audit/survey firms; commenters told CMS contracting survey firms is resource-intensive
gap_type: Supply not yet formed; incumbent survey firms are labor-priced
incumbents: Myers & Stauffer; HSAG; IPRO; Press Ganey; Atlas Systems
ai_cost_lever: Very high - calls, scripted appointment requests, directory diffing and 3-day error reporting are all automatable
key_risk: Rule rollback risk under current CMS; state/plan acceptance of AI callers; call ethics & provider burden

opportunity: Newborn screening short-term follow-up & case management system (sits beside the lab LIMS)
buyer: State public health lab / NBS follow-up program
mandate: State NBS statutes in all 50 states; RUSP condition additions; HRSA NBS grants
failure_evidence: NASEM 2025: follow-up systems are internally developed in 17 programs and Excel/other in 9; LIMS is a duopoly (Revvity 23, Natus 14). Sole-source lock-in: TN Natus NeoMetrix $760k (May 2026), NY Natus LIMS single-source
gap_type: Incumbent duopoly for LIMS; homegrown/Excel for follow-up
ai_cost_lever: Medium - workflow + HL7/FHIR result routing + AI letter/triage drafting; not instrument integration
key_risk: Long sales cycles; must interoperate with the incumbent LIMS vendor who may resist; small absolute budgets
sources: NASEM 2025 Newborn Screening in the US ch.2; TN Fiscal Review 2026-05-13; NY DOH single-source register

opportunity: Medicaid Asset Verification System (bank + real property checks for ABD applicants)
failure_evidence: MACPAC: only two portal vendors, 'lack of competition makes it difficult for states to negotiate'; one data aggregator (Accuity) in 46 states. NY sole-sourced PCG extensions 3x; NY 2025 RFP requires 5 yrs Medicaid prime experience
gap_type: Duopoly + restrictive minimum qualifications + financial-institution network moat
ai_cost_lever: Low-medium - the moat is FI data access, not software; consumer-permissioned open-banking can cover disclosed accounts only
key_risk: Statute requires searching undisclosed accounts, which needs a bank network; incumbents own it
sources: MACPAC 2020 AVS compliance brief; NY DOH RFP C042527; NY DOH single-source register

opportunity: Medicaid community-engagement (work requirement) income & exemption verification: payroll/gig connectors + exemption-document AI
mandate: OBBBA (P.L. 119-21) community engagement, CMS-2454-IFC; by 1 Jan 2027; 6-month renewals for expansion adults
failure_evidence: MACPAC Jun-2026: states fear they cannot competitively procure on the timeline and will be stuck with the current E&E vendor; NC Equifax Work Number cost $11.6M (2022) -> $22.5M (2025); CMS itself: one-offer $0.30M order to Argyle Systems (11 Sep 2026) for payroll/employment data feeding 'Emmy', CMS's centralized API verification exchange for states; urgency-justified $6.95M order to Skylight for CE state technical assistance (Jan 2026)
incumbents: Deloitte; Gainwell; Conduent; Maximus; Optum; Equifax
ai_cost_lever: High for exemption/document processing and consumer-permissioned income; low for replacing the core E&E system
key_risk: 10 incumbents pledged $600M of free/discounted tooling -> price pressure; political/litigation volatility; CMS centralizing verification (Emmy) shrinks the state-level data-verification market - aim at exemption evidence/document processing or become an Emmy data source
sources: MACPAC June 2026 ch.1; CMS vendor pledge release 29 Jan 2026; CMS-2454-IFC; USAspending 75FCMC26F0150, 75FCMC26F0036

buyer: Board of pharmacy / state health dept
mandate: State PDMP statutes; mandatory-query laws; SUPPORT Act & CDC OD2A funding
failure_evidence: Structural monopoly rather than failed RFPs: Bamboo Health (PMP AWARxE) runs ~43 of 54 PDMPs
gap_type: Incumbent monopoly; interstate hub (PMPi) owned by same vendor, RxCheck is the gov-owned alternative
ai_cost_lever: Medium - platform is commodity CRUD + ingestion; value is integrations and analytics
key_risk: Switching cost & interstate interconnect; EHR gateway network effects
sources: Bamboo Health public statements; state PDMP pages
